title: Perfect complexes are compact in the quasi-coherent derived category
statement: Let X be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Every perfect object P [def-pc-perfect-complex] of D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X) [def-pc-derived-category] is compact: for every set I and family (K_i) in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X), the canonical map \bigoplus_{i\in I} \operatorname{Hom}(P,K_i) \to \operatorname{Hom}(P,\bigoplus_{i\in I}K_i) is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Use [lem-pc-derived-tensor-unit-compact] to obtain a compact object U isomorphic to the derived tensor unit.

source.place: Proposition perfect-proposition-compact-is-perfect (Tag 09M1), proof, first paragraph; structure-sheaf case

proof.text: For perfect P use [lem-pc-perfect-tensor-hom-duality] to obtain its dual D, both tensor adjunctions, and quasi-coherent closure of both tensor functors. Restrict the adjunctions along the fully faithful inclusion of D_QCoh, with Mathlib Adjunction.restrictFullyFaithful. Thus G = D tensor - is itself a left adjoint and preserves all coproducts (Adjunction.leftAdjoint_preservesColimits). Both restricted functors are additive since G preserves binary biproducts. The right unitor identifies F(U) with P. The adjunction gives additive equivalences e_M:Hom(P,M) = Hom(U,G(M)), natural in M.

proof.text: For every family E, form the direct sum d of the e_(E_i), a bijection by DirectSum.map_injective and map_surjective. Compactness of U gives the bijection b from the sum of Hom(U,G(E_i)) to Hom(U,coproduct G(E_i)). The coproduct comparison for G is an isomorphism, so postcomposition gives a bijection t to Hom(U,G(coproduct E)). Check e_(coproduct E) composed with the canonical P-Hom comparison equals t composed with b composed with d: DirectSum.addHom_ext reduces to one summand, and adjunction naturality and the coproduct comparison inclusion identity prove it. Cancel the bijection e_(coproduct E) to conclude. Empty families use the same direct-sum universal property.
